name: ViennaRNA (Python interface)
summary: Local Python interface for RNA secondary-structure prediction, thermodynamic ensembles and RNA-RNA interactions; not the full command-line suite.

argv: import math, RNA; print(RNA.__version__); s, e = RNA.fold('GCGCUUCGCC'); assert len(s) == 10 and math.isfinite(e); print(s, e)

notes: SCOPE: this automatic route installs only the official Python interface imported as RNA. It does not provide RNAfold, RNAcofold, RNAmultifold or the full command-line suite. If the user needs those executables, stop before applying this route and use the official binary downloads or documented Bioconda route in a separate Linux/macOS environment; Windows also has official binary installers. Do not silently substitute a Python interface for a requested CLI.

The reviewed CPython 3.10-3.13 wheels cover the declared OS/architectures, not PyPy or Windows ARM64. Pip is wheel-only and will fail rather than compile source when a compatible wheel is unavailable. Wheel sizes are roughly 2-14 MB before dependencies. Linux wheels require compatible glibc or musl tags; OS/CPU matching alone does not guarantee wheel compatibility.

ViennaRNA has its own license, not this repository's MIT license: retain attribution, do not redistribute it or derived works for a fee beyond media costs, and contact the authors before including it in a commercial product. This repository distributes installation instructions, not the third-party software.

Verification imports the compiled bindings and folds one short synthetic RNA entirely offline. It checks basic execution, not prediction accuracy or suitability for protein-nucleic-acid docking or RNA 3D structure prediction. No user sequences are uploaded.
